subject: Computer science

objectives.name: Show that you understand computing facts, concepts, principles and vocabulary, and the methods and skills used to solve problems through computational thinking.
Use your computing knowledge and computational thinking methods to solve problems, and choose suitable ways to present computing information.
Develop and assess problem specifications, system requirements, success criteria, test strategies and programs. Analyse the techniques, evidence and technical explanations supporting your solution.
Apply computational thinking to build computing solutions for problems in the real world.

components.name: Computational solution (SL)

criteria.name: Problem specification
criteria.guidance: Define the problem and give requirements specific enough to test the finished thing against.

criteria.name: Planning
criteria.guidance: Show the design decisions and why you made them, not just what you built.

criteria.name: System overview
criteria.guidance: How the parts fit together. Diagrams that a reader could rebuild the structure from.

criteria.name: Development
criteria.guidance: The largest criterion and the only one assessing the product. Show techniques, not just working code.

criteria.name: Evaluation
criteria.guidance: Test against your own criterion A requirements, and say what you would do differently.

notes: 2027 guide: a 35-hour computational solution, 30 marks across five criteria, with a video submission alongside the documentation. 30% at SL, 20% at HL, same criteria at both levels.
Applies from the May 2027 session. A November 2026 candidate is still on the previous guide (34 marks, different criteria) — check the student's exam session before quoting anything.
Four of the five criteria assess process; only D assesses the finished product, with the video as the primary evidence of functionality.
Scoping is the dominant failure: a modest system that demonstrably runs outscores an ambitious one that does not.
The 2027 guide does not require a named client.

The main subject page explicitly describes last assessment 2026 and must not supply topics for this record. The linked 2027 curriculum update supplies these headings; its assessment prose and table disagree on SL weighting, so no assessment figures are taken from it.

AO1-AO4 are paraphrased from the first-assessment-2027 IB subject brief hosted by Mickiewicz Katowice and independently matched against Heidelberg International School’s 2026-28 handbook. Only the agreeing objective text is used from the handbook; its adjacent examination-duration table contains inconsistencies and is not a source for timing or weighting. Neither source publishes separate per-AO weightings, so these remain unknown.
